name: C# / .NET Patterns
description: C#/.NET patterns — async/await, LINQ, nullable reference types, dependency injection, IDisposable
content:
# C# / .NET Patterns

- Use `async`/`await` all the way through the call chain — never block on async code with `.Result` or `.Wait()`
- Enable nullable reference types (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`) and resolve all nullability warnings
- Use LINQ for collection queries but avoid deeply chained expressions — break complex queries into named steps
- Register dependencies via constructor injection using the built-in DI container — avoid the service locator pattern
- Implement `IDisposable` correctly with the dispose pattern when managing unmanaged resources, and prefer `using` declarations
- Use `record` types for immutable data transfer objects and value semantics
- Prefer pattern matching (`is`, `switch` expressions) over type casting with `as` followed by null checks
- Use `CancellationToken` in all async methods to support cooperative cancellation
- Throw specific exception types (`ArgumentNullException`, `InvalidOperationException`) — never throw base `Exception`
- Use `ILogger<T>` from Microsoft.Extensions.Logging for structured logging — avoid `Console.WriteLine` in production code
